_comment: English is the SCHEMA, not just a translation: every lookup falls back here, and a
key absent from this file does not exist as far as the app is concerned. Adding a
string means adding it here first; tests/test_i18n.py then names it as untranslated
in every other catalog until someone fills it in.
Values are PLAIN TEXT -- never markup. Jinja autoescapes t() and the browser side
assigns through textContent, so a tag in here renders as visible angle brackets.
Placeholders are {named}, and the set of names in a translation must match this
file's exactly (a test enforces it -- a dropped {machine} is a silent bug).
Keys are dotted paths written as nested objects, so a 500-key file stays reviewable.
The leading section is the page or component the string belongs to; 'common' is for
text that genuinely appears on several pages, not a dumping ground.

login.title: Sign in
login.prompt: Sign in with an authorized account to view the dashboard.

denied.title: Access denied
denied.default_message: You do not have permission to view this page.
denied.note: Permissions come from the groups you belong to. Ask an administrator to add you to a group that covers this.

dashboard.heading: Live CPU Monitor
dashboard.empty: No machines have reported in yet.

inventory.heading: Asset Inventory
inventory.intro: Every machine that is, or ever was, visible to the hub. Online machines also appear on the live Dashboard; offline ones stay here until deleted. Deleting a machine permanently removes its identity, temperature history, and fleet enrollment.
inventory.search_placeholder: Search name, asset tag, serial, service tag…
inventory.empty: No machines have reported in yet.
inventory.confirm_delete:
Permanently delete "{machine}"?

This removes its identity, all temperature history, and its fleet enrollment. This cannot be undone.

alerts.heading: Alerts
alerts.intro: Conditions that want your attention. Machines running hot — whose average temperature over the configured window is at or above the high-temperature threshold — show here and stay until you dismiss them, one card per episode, so a machine that runs hot repeatedly builds up a card per spell rather than replacing the last one. So do duplicate machines that share a serial number while both are online: the hub won't merge live machines automatically, so pick which record to keep and the others are merged into it (their temperature history is preserved).
alerts.empty: No open alerts. You're all caught up.

high_temp.title: High temperature: {machine}
_window: A sentence fragment, not a string of its own: it fills {window} in the four
bodies below so a known window reads '5-min average' and an unknown one reads
'windowed average'. Translate it as it would appear mid-sentence.
high_temp.ongoing: The {window} average {avg} °C is at or above the {threshold} °C threshold. Hot since {since}.
high_temp.ongoing_peak: The {window} average {avg} °C is at or above the {threshold} °C threshold (peak {peak} °C). Hot since {since}.
high_temp.ended: Ran at or above the {threshold} °C threshold. From {from} until {until}.
high_temp.ended_peak: Ran at or above the {threshold} °C threshold, peaking at {peak} °C ({window} average). From {from} until {until}.

duplicate.title: ⚠ Duplicate serial number: {serial}
duplicate.intro: These machines report the same serial and are both online. Choose the record to keep:
duplicate.pick_first: Pick a machine to keep first.

confirm.one:
Keep "{survivor}" and merge "{victim}" into it?

The merged machines' temperature history moves onto "{survivor}"; their duplicate records and fleet enrollments are removed. This cannot be undone.
confirm.other:
Keep "{survivor}" and merge {count} machines into it?

The merged machines' temperature history moves onto "{survivor}"; their duplicate records and fleet enrollments are removed. This cannot be undone.

audit.heading: Audit Log
audit.intro: Who did what on this hub: every command issued, machine changed, package deployed, account edited, and key touched. Append-only and not machine-scoped — entries are never rewritten or deleted, so this is the record to reach for after the fact.
audit.empty_filtered: No audit entries match these filters.

showing_recent.one: Showing the {count} most recent matching entry.
showing_recent.other: Showing the {count} most recent matching entries.

audit.load_failed: Could not load the audit log: {error}

users.heading: Users
users.intro: The people who use this console. Anyone who signs in is added automatically; you can also add someone ahead of their first login. Editing a profile here does not change what they can do — that is set by their Permission Groups.
users.search_placeholder: Search by name, username, or email
users.empty_hint: Anyone who signs in appears here automatically.
users.confirm_delete:
Remove "{user}" from the directory?

This only removes their profile. It does NOT change what they can do or whether they can sign in — that is set by their Permission Groups.
